page: Amazon Web Services r8idn.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance running on the AWS Nitro System and powered by an Intel processor operating at up to 3.9 GHz. It provisions 8 vCPUs across 4 dedicated physical cores with 2 threads per core, matched with 64.0 GB of system memory. This architecture establishes an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio, catering to compute environments where memory density is prioritized over raw core parallelism.

The instance includes 474 GB of integrated NVMe SSD local instance storage, providing low-latency ephemeral I/O without incurring external block storage network overhead. Network connectivity features a 12 Gbps baseline throughput managed via Nitro hardware offloading. The system does not include discrete GPUs and provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Bundling fast local NVMe storage with high per-core RAM offers qualitative cost efficiencies for operational layers that demand high-speed caching and intermediate data persistence. Because local NVMe media is ephemeral, persistent storage architectures require external synchronization or supplemental storage volumes. The r8idn.2xlarge is structured for in-memory databases, memory-resident search indices, key-value stores, and transactional database nodes.
description: Amazon Web Services r8idn.2xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Nitro System and driven by a 3.9 GHz Intel processor. It delivers 8 vCPUs over 4 dedicated physical cores alongside 64.0 GB of RAM, maintaining an 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio. In addition to high memory capacity, the instance integrates 474 GB of direct-attached local NVMe SSD instance store, paired with a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. The system contains no discrete GPUs and allocates zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses. By combining dense memory with fast local solid-state storage, r8idn.2xlarge delivers low-latency disk and RAM access for data-heavy operations. The integrated local NVMe volume minimizes reliance on external network volumes for temporary caches, though data durability requires persistent storage architectures. The configuration fits in-memory caching systems, transactional databases, real-time analytics engines, and memory-bound data pipelines requiring dedicated processing resources.
